narration: More than two thousand years ago,
main_visual: Extreme macro: one bronze gear begins to turn

narration: someone in ancient Greece built a machine to predict the sky.
main_visual: A second gear engages; pull back through the stack to the dial plate with a faint star/zodiac ring
motion_graphics: A MACHINE TO PREDICT THE SKY. (proposed, from 3.9 s)

narration: Made of bronze and packed with gears,
main_visual: Macro tracking through the bronze gear stack

narration: it tracked the cycles of the Sun and Moon
main_visual: Soft back-dial plate with the Sun-and-Moon diagram
Eclipse-cycle schematic over the dial plate
object_movement: Eclipse glyph lights on the cycle ring

narration: Found in a shipwreck near Antikythera in 1901,
main_visual: Underwater: light shaft, sandy seabed, amphora shards, timber ribs

narration: it became known as the Antikythera Mechanism.
main_visual: Corroded lump rises toward the light; colour warms
Macro of a corroded fragment with teeth under crust
Fragments slide into an exploded view of clean gears
The exploded stack settles into the assembled mechanism; slow glide
motion_graphics: ABOUT ONE THIRD SURVIVES (optional, needs approval)

narration: But its full design is still debated.
main_visual: Outer gear groups begin to ghost to Scientific Cyan wireframes
Whole sections fade, leaving empty space around the solid core

narration: and researchers are still piecing together how it worked.
main_visual: Ghost gears reassemble slowly around the surviving core

narration: Often called the world’s oldest known analogue computer.
main_visual: Low orbit around the completed reconstruction in its case
motion_graphics: THE ANTIKYTHERA MECHANISM (39.1 s); THE OLDEST KNOWN ANALOGUE COMPUTER (41.2 s); SCIENTIFIC TERM: MECHANICAL CALCULATOR (43.2 s)

narration: A small machine built to model an immense sky.
main_visual: Calm pull-back to a wide of the small machine against a starred sky
motion_graphics: EPOCH & ELEMENT; The Forces That Shaped Our World. (from 46.0 s)
